label: <DEL> step of short (L=3) sequences, esp. those starting with i/a/j/o/u/v/g/p
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass at phase 1, recall_idx 0); never in original or copy phases. Even there it is sparse (0.4% of delimiter steps). 82% of mass is at L=3, 13% at L=9, a little at L=4. Within L=3 it is modulated by token identity: strongest when the first original token (the token about to be output) is i (36% of mass), then a, j, u, v, g, o, p; prev tokens a/p/d/g also raise it, and digit-containing sequences fire less. Top examples: a i a, i t a, j i a. Does not fire for L=6-7 and rarely for L=5/8. Token-identity dependence is graded and not cleanly captured, so precision stays low (~0.35 dev).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: i, u, j, a, v, o; least: c, -, h, 2) and the third original token (most: a, p, k, w, o, i; least: h, z, x, e); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=3, L=3, t=3.
